title: To Implement Acquisition Transformation, Empower Military Mavericks
gist: Former DIU insiders argue the Pentagon already has the authorities for commercial-first buying but lacks trained people, and that the Defense Innovation Unit (now ~$1B/yr and the designated commercial-adoption center of excellence) should become a 'weapons school' that selects, trains, credentials and redeploys acquisition mavericks with career incentives; they cite Saronic's $392M contract and only 4% of Navy budget on unmanned vessels as evidence of both promise and under-reallocation.

insights.claim: For the past decade the Pentagon has had the legal authorities to buy commercially derived technology at speed and scale but not enough people who know how to use them.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: The bottleneck for defense-tech startup revenue is acquisition workforce execution, not legislation.
insights.quote: the Pentagon has had the authorities to buy commercially derived technologies at speed and scale, but not enough people who know how to use those authorities
insights.locator: For the last decade, the Pentagon

insights.claim: The acquisition and resourcing system incentivizes fear and compliance more than sourcing, prototyping and scaling commercial technologies, which is why reallocation has lagged despite policy.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Policy announcements overstate near-term commercial adoption; track actual program-of-record transitions instead.
insights.quote: the acquisition and resourcing system incentivizes fear and compliance more than it encourages the sourcing, prototyping, and scaling

insights.claim: DIU Principal Deputy Director Matt Shortal testified in September that reports indicate just four percent of the Navy's budget is allocated to unmanned vessels, evidence the U.S. has failed to reallocate resources to Third Offset priorities.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Low unmanned share implies large headroom for budget reallocation toward autonomous maritime vendors.
insights.quote: just four percent of the Navy’s budget is allocated to unmanned vessels

insights.claim: Transforming the Defense Acquisition University into a Warfighting Acquisition University risks being a rename, because centralized certification sets a baseline but does not prove mastery of negotiating commercially viable deals or transitioning technology.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Skepticism that the Acquisition Transformation Strategy's workforce fix will speed contracting on its own.
insights.quote: Certification establishes a baseline, but it does not demonstrate mastery.

themes.theme: DIU history: mavericks punished, then vindicated

insights.claim: DIU originated from Chuck Hagel's November 2014 Third Offset Strategy and was set up as a Silicon Valley storefront by Ash Carter; in 2016 its three-person team created the commercial solutions opening process using other transaction agreements.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: CSO/OTA is the contracting rail through which venture-backed defense startups win fast awards.

insights.claim: From 2016 to 2024 DIU was secluded, budget-constrained and dependent on mission partners; its warnings about small drones threatening parked aircraft, drones in the Nagorno-Karabakh War and proliferating commercial satellite imagery were routinely dismissed.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Institutional resistance delayed adoption of technologies that later proved decisive, a pattern that may repeat for current emerging tech.

insights.claim: Servicemembers who worked at DIU often had their careers harmed upon returning to the services, including one author whose military career was permanently derailed as DIU's first warfighter-in-residence.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Career penalties shrink the pool of capable commercial-tech buyers inside the military.
insights.quote: it also meant permanently derailing the author’s military career

insights.claim: Several of DIU's best projects (maritime ISR, construction-scale additive manufacturing, peacetime indications and warning) came from coincidental alignment with vendors like SailDrone, ICON Technology and Capella Space whose founders had not imagined the military as a customer; Capella imagery showed Russia was about to invade Ukraine in February 2022.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Dual-use commercial firms can become defense winners unexpectedly; commercial satellite imagery proved strategically valuable.
insights.quote: imagery from Capella’s satellites showed the world that Russia was about to invade Ukraine
insights.locator: Some of the unit’s most successful

insights.claim: After the Ukraine war validated agile software, small drones and space-based sensing, Congress under Rep. Ken Calvert codified DIU's director as a principal staff assistant to the secretary of defense and appropriated almost $1 billion per year.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: A ~$1B/yr DIU budget is a durable funding pool for commercial defense-tech vendors.
insights.quote: appropriated an annual budget of almost $1 billion

insights.claim: A 2024 DIU solicitation for small strike-capable unmanned surface vessels led to Saronic Technologies receiving a $392 million contract, with the vessels since used to rescue downed pilots and strike an Iranian submarine.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Combat-validated USVs strengthen Saronic's position and the autonomous-maritime category.
insights.quote: Saronic Technologies receiving a $392 million contract

insights.claim: DIU's 2024 low-cost cruise missile solicitation awarded agreements to Zone 5 Technologies and Anduril Industries and is now an Air Force program of record.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Program-of-record status signals sustained production revenue for low-cost cruise missile makers.
insights.quote: is now a program of record with the Air Force

insights.claim: Since January 2025 the Pentagon has mandated CSOs and other transactions as default for the Software Acquisition Pathway (March 2025), designated acquisition a warfighting function with commercial-first as the preferred approach (November 2025), and named DIU the department's center of excellence for commercial technology adoption (January).
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Policy tailwinds for non-traditional defense vendors are now formal; execution is the remaining risk.

themes.theme: DIU as a weapons school for acquisition

insights.claim: The authors propose DIU become the department's weapons school for commercial technology acquisition, modeled on Top Gun and the Air Force Weapons School: select promising servicemembers, train rigorously, credential visibly and send them back to teach others.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: If adopted, would broaden the number of offices capable of fast commercial awards, widening startup addressable demand.
insights.quote: the department’s weapons school for commercial technology acquisition
insights.locator: This article argues that the Defense

insights.claim: The proposed six-step pipeline is: select mavericks for temperament and reputation, run a formal course, use a see-it-do-it-teach-it probation leading to OTA warrants, credential graduates, place them in key portfolio acquisition offices, and reconvene at an annual conference.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: A concrete reform blueprint to watch for adoption in DIU or service policy.
insights.locator: To meet the moment, the unit

insights.claim: The determinative incentive is career credit: a special experience identifier and Joint Duty Assignment List credit so DIU time boosts promotion, which the mavericks who built DIU never had.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Career incentives are the lever that would make commercial-first buying scale beyond a handful of enthusiasts.
insights.quote: Time at the unit should enhance specially selected servicemembers’ careers, an incentive the mavericks who built the unit never had.

insights.claim: Graduates should be placed in offices buying commercial tech, such as the Air Force PAE for C3 and Battle Management, the Navy PAE for Robotics and Autonomous Systems, the Army PAE Maneuver Ground, SOCOM's PEO SOF Warrior and service rapid capabilities offices.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: These portfolio offices are the likely centers of commercial-first demand for defense-tech vendors.

insights.claim: Absent incentives for scaling commercial technology, acquisition transformation will not be implemented effectively and servicemembers pursuing commercial-first approaches will keep risking their careers.
insights.speaker: Ben McNally and Donald Gansberger
insights.so_what: Discount headline reform; adoption speed hinges on personnel incentives.
